confidence_rationale: Review arguing that laughter is primarily a social emotion. Observational work (Provine; Vettin & Todt) finds that most laughter happens in conversation after ordinary statements rather than jokes; people are ~30x more likely to laugh with others present; and volitional (social) laughter is acoustically and neurally distinct from evoked (involuntary) laughter, in humans and in chimpanzees. This weakens MECH-110 as a claim about LAUGHTER in general: most laughter has no evident incongruity-resolution antecedent. The claim survives only if restricted to evoked laughter. The social-bonding, contagion and stress-regulation functions partly support the V5-scoped social extension.
failure_signatures: Most naturally occurring laughter follows ordinary conversational statements, not jokes or resolved incongruities, so incongruity + resolution cannot be a necessary antecedent of laughter in general.

Volitional and evoked laughter are dissociable acoustically and neurally (e.g., hypothalamus for reactive laughter, prefrontal cortex for perception of voluntary laughter), so a single tag-cycling mechanism is at best a model of one laughter type.
Laughter is strongly audience-dependent (~30x more likely with others present), which a purely intra-agent threat/resolution cycle does not predict.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Laughter is a social emotion occurring mostly in interaction, associated with bonding, agreement, affection and emotion regulation; most conversational laughter follows statements rather than jokes; social (voluntary) laughter is distinct from evoked (involuntary) laughter in humans and chimpanzees and in brain imaging.
mapping.ree_translation: Constrains MECH-110's scope: the threat-activation / safe-resolution cycling account can at most cover evoked (involuntary, humour-driven) laughter. The contagion and bonding findings bear on the V5-scoped social extension (group laughter as shared 'threat absent' signalling / clock entrainment) but do not test entrainment of any planning clock.
mapping.mapping_caveat: A short opinion-style review summarising others' observational data, not new evidence. Absence of an overt joke does not prove absence of a micro-incongruity or social-threat resolution in conversational laughter, so the weakening is on scope rather than a refutation of the mechanism for evoked laughter.
mapping.source_context: Human conversational and observational studies, neuroimaging of voluntary vs involuntary laughter, and chimpanzee tickle vs play laughter; TICS forum-style review.

confidence_components.notes: Weakens the generality of MECH-110's title claim ('Laughter is ...') more than its humour-structure prediction. Suggested narrowing: restrict to evoked laughter, treat volitional/social laughter as a separate channel.
